scope: The exact 16-image public-route matrix: unchanged reviewed selection screens plus the four changed initial-gameplay screens in desktop, narrow desktop, phone landscape, and phone portrait. The changed gameplay PNGs were independently reviewed at original resolution after machine gates passed.
resolvedFindings: The authored workshop, lanterns, crates, floor, and actors now establish a recognizably Diablo-like dark-gothic scene rather than an empty test arena.
The former Hexer/Vanguard/workshop overlap is resolved: Vanguard, Stonekin, and Ashfang have clean silhouettes in all four gameplay profiles.
The workshop apron, southern lane, and gap between the two opening monsters read as honestly navigable, matching the solid collision and real input tests.
Touch controls remain clear of the encounter in portrait and landscape, and the narrow-desktop composition balances the landmark and actors cleanly.
rejectedFindings: Ashfang still reads more like a prone corpse than a living combatant; its thin health line carries too much of the active-threat meaning.
The solid black gate bays above and to the right of the workshop remain conspicuous rectangular seams and look like unfinished tile cutouts.
Character sprites remain softer and more haloed than the crisp high-frequency workshop art.
Wide desktop and phone-landscape compositions leave too much inactive rocky ground while concentrating authored complexity in one upper-center cluster.
Plain floating enemy health lines are stylistically unfinished beside the ornate sprite-based world and HUD, and mobile framing still clips authored lantern/workshop edges.
promotionRule: This rejection applies only while both the contract and ordered screenshot-set hashes match. Any pixel or contract change invalidates it and returns the gallery to candidate; no machine metric can override a matching rejection.
